newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZSE panel censures Max for non disclosure.
newsitem.headline: NZSE panel censures Max for non disclosure.

text.p: The New Zealand Stock Exchange Market Surveillance Panel said on Tuesday it had censured Max Resources Ltd for failure to properly disclose market sensitive information.
Earlier the exchange had lifted a suspension of trade on Max saying it was satisfied the company was now informing the market fairly.

The exchange on March 24 inquired about Max's share price rise to 80 NZ cents from 49 cents on February 3 and Max executive director Mike Langoulant responded saying he knew no reason why the company's share price had risen.

The exchange said it then received information that one of Max's directors (Jeff Verheggen) had visited several Auckland brokers' analysts and had provided them with financial forecasts and information about Max's prospects.

This included a draft of the unpublished information memorandum required by the panel under listing rules in relation to the proposed change to the nature of its business from a gold mining investment company to an organic fertiliser manufacturer.

"On inquiry, it was apparent that this was indeed the case, despite initial denials by Mr Jeff Verheggen and also by Mr Langoulant, who has subsequently advised the Panel that he had relied on assurances received from Mr Verheggen," the exchange said.

"The panel takes the view that the above represents a flagrant breach of the Listing Rules and hereby censures Max, and Mr Verheggen in particular and Mr Langoulant to a lesser extent, for their respective roles in this matter."
NZSE panel secretary Philippe Leloir said past censures had always had a significant impact on the affected company.

"Don't underestimate the velvet touch," he told Reuters. They think it is nothing worse than death having their names highlighted like this. They think it is the worst thing that would happen to their reputations. Out of anything we can do that (censure) hurts most," Leloir said.
